title: Write-Ahead Log
subtitle: Log the change to disk before you apply it, and choose how often to force that log to disk
motto: Write it down first, then do it
keyInsight: A write-ahead log makes a crash recoverable by replay, and how often you fsync decides how many acknowledged writes a crash can still lose.

decisions.title: Show the log without fsync as the failure
decisions.description: The failure frame keeps the log but skips the forced flush, because that is the setting that looks safe and still loses acknowledged writes.
decisions.alternatives: Stopping at 'we have a WAL' would hide that durability depends on fsync.

decisions.title: Report fsync demand against the disk
decisions.description: The fsync-busy metric goes above 100% when commits ask for more forced flushes than the disk can do, which motivates group commit.
decisions.alternatives: Showing only commit latency would not explain why real databases batch their fsyncs.
